newsitem.title: UK: UK POLICE FIND NO BOMBS AFTER "NATIONAL" ALERT.
newsitem.headline: UK POLICE FIND NO BOMBS AFTER "NATIONAL" ALERT.

text.p: Police said on Saturday they had carried out three controlled explosions after a bomb alert forced the cancellation of the Grand National, Britain's best-known horse race, but had found no bombs.
Race organisers said they had contingency plans to re-run the race on Monday but this had to be confirmed after talks with owners and trainers.

Police Assistant Chief Constable Paul Stephenson told a news conference that three controlled explosions had been carried out at Aintree racecourse after a bomb alert forced the evacuation of 60,000 racegoers, but all had been found to be "innocent".
He said the security operation was continuing and thousands of cars and coaches stilled trapped inside the perimeter of the course would have to remain there at least until Sunday.
Clerk of the Course Chris Barnett said there were contingency plans to hold the 150th running of the race, one of Britain's best-loved sporting events, on Monday, but this still had to be confirmed.

Police received two coded warnings just 30 minutes before the race was due to start. Prime Minister John Major and other political leaders have condemned the bomb warnings as the work of the Irish Republican Army, which is fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
